subject: Next steps: latency & throughput playbook for Nimbus AI trial
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Mike Holt <mike@nimbl.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: latency & throughput playbook for Nimbus AI trial

Hi Mike — thanks again for the 30-minute sync earlier. Thought I’d capture the concrete items we discussed so everyone (internal + Nimbus) has the same checklist. Short version at the top, details below.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: p95 latency spikes during streaming/user-interactive flows + cost from inefficient batching
- Target: p95 <= 200ms for interactive paths, sustained 400 rps (peaks to 2k) with sub-150ms token latencies where possible
- Immediate next steps: share traces & sample requests, spin a 2-week trial with 2-GPU and 4-GPU configs, technical deep-dive next Thu (engineers only)

Notes from today's call (paraphrased):
- Pain points
  - Users see stuttering and partial responses in the chat UX when concurrency climbs; appears to be KV-cache misses and cold-start latencies for some multi-turn flows.
  - Current stack: in-house Triton endpoints (GCP us-west1), a basic prefix cache, and an application-side request fan-in. No automated batching across requests today.
  - SLA ask: Nimbus wants reliability for interactive experiences (p95 target) and predictable burst handling for marketing/demo spikes.

- Success criteria for an initial trial
  1) p95 (end-to-end from request to first token) <= 200ms for 95% of interactive calls during a 1h synthetic load that simulates production mix
  2) Drop in mean cost-per-response by >= 25% via batching/caching/quantization suggestions (measured on the same workload)
  3) No more than 1 visible UX interruption per 10k interactive requests (measure by synthetic user traces)

- Technical constraints you mentioned
  - Multi-region traffic but primary traffic in us-west.
  - Must avoid customer data egress; trial stays in customer GCP project (private deployment) or Dedicated with VPC peering.
  - Procurement window: Nimbus expects procurement signed within 6–8 weeks if trial is successful.

Immediate asks from Redwood (what we need from Nimbus to get the trial running)
1) Three representative request logs & one sample trace (JSON) from a typical interactive session (we'll use to size batching & cache heuristics)
2) Open a short NATed test endpoint or provide sample payloads and tokenization rules
3) Point person for engineering scheduling (you mentioned Lara on your infra team)

Planned Redwood deliverables for the trial
- Trial environment with 2-GPU and 4-GPU profiles (TBD kernel/quantization).
- Baseline run and one optimized run with suggested batching/cache flags; we'll provide config diffs.
- Post-trial report showing p95, token latencies, throughput, and cost delta.

Attachments: Redwood-SLA-template.pdf (SLA language we can start with), trial-queue-config.yaml (example queue/batching knobs).

Proposed calendar items
- Technical deep-dive (engineers only): Thu Jul 8, 10:00–11:00 PT — Markus to lead kernel/serving discussion
- Trial kick-off: Mon Jul 12 — environment up and baseline run scheduled that week

If that aligns, I'll follow up with a short kickoff invite and share the trial checklist.

Thanks,
Sean
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Mike Holt <mike@nimbl.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Lara Chen <lara@nimbl.ai>, procurement@nimbl.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: latency & throughput playbook for Nimbus AI trial

Sean — really helpful write-up, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed targets: our product PMs are comfortable with p95 <= 180–200ms for conversational first-token latency. We tend to see mid-tier spikes around launch events (up to ~2k concurrent active users) but the normal steady-state is 300–500 rps.
- Cold starts: the bigger issue for us is the cold-start behavior of certain long-session flows (multi-turn with long KV caches). We suspect the current Triton setup evicts KV state aggressively which is making tail latency worse.

Quick answers to your asks:
1) Request logs: attached is one anonymized session export (session_export_0626.json) and a small sample trace — should be enough for an initial sizing pass.
2) Test endpoint: we can spin up a NATed test endpoint in our GCP project for the trial, but procurement needs the detail of what network & IAM access Redwood requires.
3) Point person: Lara Chen (cc'd) will own infra coordination.

Procurement note: procurement team has started preliminary review. We will likely need a short SOC2 addendum and the SLA template you attached will help. Timeline still looks like 6 weeks if trial shows expected improvements.

Questions for Redwood before the deep-dive:
- Do you have performance expectations (throughput per GPU) for your 2-GPU vs 4-GPU baseline configs for models of our size?
- Can you outline the approach to streaming UX — do you preserve partial tokens and refill gaps client-side or rely on server streaming?

I'll circulate timing options for the deep-dive once Lara confirms availability.

—Mike
CTO, Nimbus AI
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Next steps: latency & throughput playbook for Nimbus AI trial

Forwarding Mike's note — a few internal action items I want on the board before the technical deep-dive: 

Action items
- Markus: please prepare a short doc (1–2 pages) that sketches expected QPS-per-GPU numbers for the Llama-ish family at 4k context, and the expected differences with INT8 quant and continuous batching on. If you can include estimates for 2-GPU and 4-GPU baselines that'd be ideal.
- I'll draft a trial runbook: baseline workload generation script, pass/fail SLO checks, instrumentation points (traces/metrics).
- Sean: I'll need the HubSpot deal id and a single owner you want on the trial so we know who signs off on success criteria.

Also: recommend we enable prefix/KV caching with a warmer policy for the trial to reduce first-turn misses. That tends to help customer UX quickly.

I'll attach the trial runbook skeleton to the shared drive once the doc is in shape.

—Monica
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Mike Holt <mike@nimbl.ai>
Cc: Lara Chen <lara@nimbl.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, procurement@nimbl.ai

Subject: Re: Next steps: latency & throughput playbook for Nimbus AI trial

Mike — great, thanks for the attachments and for looping Lara/procurement. Confirming the plan and owners from our side: 
- Redwood trial owner: Sean Gallagher (me) — I will be the point for commercial & scheduling.
- Technical lead: Markus Klein (cc'd) — will lead the deep-dive and sizing discussion.
- CS/Success runbook: Monica Patel — will own trial success criteria and post-trial report.

Proposed deep-dive times (PT): Thu Jul 8, 10:00–11:00; Fri Jul 9, 14:00–15:00. Markus — can you pick one and we will lock it with Lara?

Deliverables before kickoff:
- Nimbus: anonymized traces & one representative session export (we've got this).
- Nimbus/procurement: list of required network/IAM permissions for the NATed test endpoint (Lara).
- Redwood: trial environment spec, 2-GPU and 4-GPU perf expectations doc (Markus), and the trial runbook skeleton (Monica).

I'll send an invite once Markus confirms a deep-dive slot. Looking forward to making this trial low-friction — biggest wins are usually from small cache/batching changes.

Best,
Sean
